problem: Model-based RL world models (e.g. DreamerV2) learn state representations via reconstruction, which cannot separate task-relevant from irrelevant style features, so policies fail under out-of-distribution scenes and textures and in sim-to-real transfer. Naive contrastive losses collapse in world models because representation learning is decoupled from the policy and gets no supervisory signal.
motivation: Robust, sample-efficient visual control needs state abstractions that keep causal (content) variables and ignore spurious style. Invariance-based causal discovery usually needs multiple environments, while the authors want a single-environment approach that uses augmentation as the intervention, and depth as the geometric signal needed for navigation.
key_idea: Learn a DreamerV2-style world model whose encoder is trained with an InfoNCE contrastive loss across style augmentations (interventions) of RGB, stabilized by an intervention-invariant depth reconstruction auxiliary task (depth is needed only in training).
insight: Contrastive loss alone collapses inside a world model: removing depth reconstruction (WMC - AR - D) drops iGibson total SR to 0.03 at 100k and 0.7 at 500k. Depth is invariant to RGB style augmentations, so it supplies the supervisory signal. Replacing depth with RGB reconstruction (WMC - D + I) cuts SR at 500k from 47.2 to 19.1. Contrastive learning adds gains beyond augmentation and depth alone (DreamerV2 - I + D + DA gets 33.2 SR at 500k vs WMC 47.26).
method: Style intervention module: data augmentation (spatial jitter via pad + random crop, Gaussian blur, color jitter, grayscale, cutout) produces two correlated views of each observation; no resize, to keep object size/distance relations intact

Invariant encoder: DreamerV2 CNN encoder yields s~_t from RGB, concatenated with task observation features (goal, position, velocities; two 32-unit dense layers); the contrastive loss is applied right after the encoder
Contrastive loss: InfoNCE with a bilinear projection head, momentum key encoder (EMA 0.999, as in MoCo/BYOL); frames sliced every 5th step in an episode to reduce similarity between negatives
Depth reconstruction auxiliary task: decoder predicts depth from the latent state s_t (depth used only in training); replaced by RGB reconstruction for DMControl
World model (RSSM) with categorical latents: representation, transition, reward and depth models trained jointly with L_WM = contrastive + depth + reward - beta*KL
Controller: DreamerV2 actor-critic trained in imagined latent rollouts (horizon 15)
Action replay: texture randomization used as an alternative intervention (replaying the same actions under different textures); ablated as 'AR'

setting.backbone: DreamerV2 world model (RSSM) + actor-critic, with added contrastive loss and depth decoder (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: RL interaction in simulator only: 100k or 500k env steps on 12 iGibson 1.0 training scenes (Table lists 12 scene names; text says five); no extra or web data
setting.observation: monocular RGB 120x160 + task info (goal location, current location, linear/angular velocities); depth only during training
setting.action_space: continuous: rotation (radians) and forward distance (meters) for a Turtlebot
setting.privileged: depth used during training only (auxiliary target); none at test time. Goal location and robot pose come as task observation.

numbers.eval_set_note: held-out scenes Ihlen_0_int, Ihlen_1_int, Rs_int with held-out textures; 3 seeds averaged
numbers.extra: 100k environment steps; action replay texture randomization used in training

numbers.eval_set_note: held-out scenes Ihlen_0_int, Ihlen_1_int, Rs_int with held-out textures; 3 seeds averaged
numbers.extra: 500k environment steps; action replay texture randomization used in training

numbers.eval_set_note: five Gibson scenes (Ihlen, Muleshoe, Uvalda, Noxapater, McDade); trained on iGibson textures; per-scene results only, no total

numbers_note: Benchmarks are custom (iGibson 1.0 OoD PointGoal split created by the authors; Gibson transfer). DMControl scores are in Table 3 but omitted (not navigation). SPL is printed as a fraction (0-1) in the paper.
results: On held-out iGibson scenes and textures, WMC reaches SR 22.3 at 100k and 47.26 at 500k, well ahead of CURL (4.6 / 31.4), DreamerV2 (1.3 / 1.4) and RAD (0.5 / 36.3). On Gibson sim-to-real perception transfer it beats RAD and CURL in all scenes at 100k and 4 of 5 at 500k (McDade favours CURL, 53.8 vs 50.7). On DMControl it is competitive with CURL but often worse.
limitations: Depth-based invariance is specific to navigation; on DMControl without depth, WMC is only on par and often below CURL and other baselines
Training time is about twice that of DreamerV2; hidden confounders are not handled; better ways to intervene on style are left to future work
Sim-to-real is only tested as Gibson scans in simulation (controller in simulator), not on a real robot; the ablation shows action replay matters (SR 47.2 vs 27.8 at 500k)
